title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility layer fully in parity with /v1/chat.completions semantics for params/roles/stop/logprobs and to harden streaming + function/tool calling with consistent response formatting. This PR consolidates multiple prior compatibility gaps discovered during customer onboarding and internal evals: missing/ambiguous handling of 'roles' in system/user/assistant sequences, stop token behavior combined with streaming, exposing token-level logprobs in the OpenAI shape, and response formatting differences that break downstream tool-call handlers.

What changed (summary):
- Add explicit mapping from OpenAI chat message roles to Redwood internal role enum and back; preserve original role strings when present to maintain round-trip compatibility.
- Implement 'stop' token semantics for both sync and streamed responses; streaming now emits final 'finish_reason' consistent with OpenAI behavior when stop sequences are matched mid-stream.
- Expose top_logprobs and token-level logprobs in the OpenAI-compatible response (field names and shapes aligned). Note: we clip/normalize scores and document limits.
- Response formatting: unify content vs delta fields for streamed responses so clients see consistent 'choices[].message' content in both streaming and non-streaming modes. Implemented a deterministic finalization step for structured outputs to avoid truncated JSON in streams.
- Tool/function calling: stabilize streaming tool call boundaries and provide a 'tool_call' delta type for partial tool invocations; add tests and examples showing how to reconstruct tool invocations from streams.
- API params: support OpenAI-style top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, logit_bias, and n; map them onto Redwood runtime config with validation and warnings when unsupported combinations are requested.
- Tests & docs: 60+ unit/integration tests added to the eval-harness and redwood-sdk-* examples demonstrating parity; new docs page in redwood-docs describing compatibility caveats.

Files changed (high level):
- core/api/openai_compat/chat_adapter.py: role mapping, param validation, stop handling, logprob shaping
- serving/streaming/stream_coordinator.py: streaming semantics, delta types, finish_reason behavior
- serving/streaming/tool_call_reassembler.py: reconstruct partial tool call streams into canonical tool_call objects
- sdk/python/openai_compat_client.py: example usage and integration tests
- eval-harness/tests/test_openai_chat_parity.py: large test matrix for params/roles/stop/streaming/formatting
- redwood-docs/openai-compatibility.md: docs additions and examples

Testing and CI:
- CI matrix includes unit tests, integration tests against a local runtime, and a lightweight end-to-end smoke test that validates streamed vs non-streamed equivalence for a set of prompts. Initial CI run failed on a flaky streaming ordering test; rerun after adding a retry and ordering guard fixed the failure. Final CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior unchanged for existing Redwood API users. OpenAI-compatible mode is opt-in via the compatibility flag in the request. When enabled we apply the compatibility mapping and emit additional OpenAI-shaped fields.
- Added a feature flag (openai_compat_v1) to allow staged rollout per-tenant. Gradual rollout planned over two weeks with monitoring dashboards in Redwood Console for latency, error rates, and mismatch rates against non-compat responses.

Checklist:
- [x] Role mapping implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Stop tokens handled in streaming and sync paths
- [x] top_logprobs/logprobs shapes validated against canonical fixtures
- [x] Streaming tool/function call stability and reconstruction tested
- [x] Docs and SDK examples updated
- [x] Performance tests to ensure <2% p50 latency regression in common configs

Notes:
- There are a couple of minor behavioral differences intentionally documented: 1) when logprobs are requested for extremely long sequences we cap per-request memory and return a truncated logprobs array with a warning header; 2) some rare, adversarial token sequences combined with aggressive batching may cause slightly different tokenization boundaries — we've documented this and added an opt-out.

Related: ENG-1634 (streaming stability improvements), ENG-1970 (tool-calls stabilization), DOC-512 (openai compat docs).
commits: Initial implementation: role mapping & param translation (chat_adapter) – 8 files
Streaming deltas and finish_reason handling – 4 files
Tool-call stream reassembler and example – 3 files
Fix: ordering guard for streaming tests (flaky) – test only
Perf tuning: minor kernel selection tweak to keep latency stable
review_comments:
Samir Patel: Nice consolidation — two nits: (1) can we document the memory cap behavior for logprobs in the API reference (not just the docs page)? (2) prefer explicit enum mapping instead of relying on string passthrough in chat_adapter.py

Priya Raman (author): +1 on doc placement; added api reference section and explicit enum with fallback to preserve unknown roles. Updated tests accordingly.

Dana Liu: The streaming finish_reason change looks correct, but please add an integration test for concurrent stop sequences (overlapping stop tokens across batching).

Priya Raman: Added integration test in eval-harness and a protective ordering guard in stream_coordinator.
release_notes: Opt-in OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: params (top_p, penalties, logit_bias, n), role handling, stop token parity (stream + sync), logprobs shape (top_logprobs), streaming tool/function call stability, and response formatting fixes. Opt-in via openai_compat_v1 feature flag. See redwood-docs/openai-compatibility.md for details.
